text:
zara: quick Q from the pricing block — can someone summarize the practical difference between rate limits and quotas for customers?

cole: rate limits = realtime throttles (reqs/sec, concurrency). quotas = longer window caps (tokens/month, embeddings/month). both apply to keys; trial keys usually have stricter values.

meera: follow-up: are embeddings and generation counted from separate counters or the same pool? customers keep asking.

cole: separate by default. we surface pooled credits as a special billing account flag for promos.

orion: what happens mid-stream if a job hits quota? do we let it finish or cut it off? need a clear expectation for SDKs.

cole: policy: if the org is within a grace window (configurable, default 300s) in-flight requests are allowed to complete and responses may include header X-Quota-Status: soft_limit_exceeded. after grace, new requests return 429/quota_exceeded. 402 used only for billing failures.

zara: do we ever auto-charge trials when they want more quota? sales wants clarity.

meera: no auto-charge for trials. paid customers with card on file can opt into auto-topup for quota add-ons (opt-in). for pilots we do manual quota increases authorized by sales/finance.

zara: any way to expose remaining quota programmatically so apps can show "X left this month"? mobile folks asked.

orion: proposing 2 options: opt-in response header X-Redwood-Remaining: tokens=12345;embeddings=80 (only returned for requests authenticated with an org key and enabled in console) and an admin-only endpoint GET /v1/orgs/:id/usage for detailed data. header avoids an extra call; endpoint for dashboards.

meera: security note — header must never be returned for public or client-side keys. usage endpoint requires admin scope and will redact PII.

zara: credits question — do promo credits increase quotas or just offset invoices? finance needs this on the FAQ.

finance-bot: system: promo credits reduce the billing balance by default. converting credits into temporary quota increases is a manual, auditable flow handled by billing/ops.

zara: could we make that self-serve for growth customers? ops might complain though.

meera: considering a limited self-serve toggle for vetted accounts with strict caps and audit logs. not GA yet.

orion: error payloads — can we standardize so SDKs can reliably parse?

cole: agreed. canonical responses: 429 rate limit -> {"error":"rate_limited","retry_after":int}; 429 quota -> {"error":"quota_exceeded","quota_type":"tokens|embeddings","grace_remaining":int}; 402 -> {"error":"insufficient_funds","detail":string}. we'll publish examples in API docs.

zara: can we include an admin_url in the quota response so UIs can link to upgrade flow?

cole: yes — include admin_url when the key owner requests it. sample body we'll add to docs.

all-hands-bot: follow-ups created: #9001 docs:quota-and-errors, #9002 billing:promo-to-quota-policy, #9003 infra:usage-endpoint-auth

zara: last one — Dedicated customers: do they get the same soft grace behavior?

meera: Dedicated maps quotas to committed capacity in contract. we can enable the same headers/webhooks but defaults are tighter and SRE owns emergency scaling.

orion: noted. i'll surface these follow-ups to CS and SDK teams. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
